sentences: Merlin–Arthur verification combines a classical witness with an efficient randomized check.
Applying an existential quantifier to an ordinary BPP language imposes an additional bounded-error condition on every witness-input pair.
In an MA protocol, by contrast, unsuccessful witnesses on a yes-instance may have intermediate acceptance probabilities.
This question asks whether those different promise conventions nevertheless define the same class.
The distinction matters when building classical or quantum verification hierarchies, because moving quantifiers across probabilistic tests can silently strengthen the requirements on a verifier.
